units.1: Chemical Reactions: Rate of chemical reactions, variable affecting the reaction rate, order of reaction, rate constant, elementary and non-elementary reaction mechanism. Temperature dependency from thermodynamics, Arrhenius collision and activated complex theories.
units.2: Integral and differential methods for analyzing kinetic data, Interpretation of constant volume batch reactor data for zero, first, second and third order reactions, Half life period, Irreversible reaction in parallel and series, Autocatalytic reaction.
units.3: Interpretation of reactor data in variable volume batch reactions, Design equations for batch, plug flow, back mix flow and semi batch reactors for isothermal, adiabatic homogeneous reaction.
units.4: Space velocity and residence time in flow reactors, Design of batch, plug flow and mixed flow reactors for first and second order single reactions, Size comparison of single reactors like batch, plug flow and CSTR for first and second order single reactions. Multiple reactor systems, Plug flow reactions in series and for parallel equal sized CSTR's in series. Best arrangement of different type of reactors.
units.5: Temperature and pressure effects for single reaction, Optimal temperature progression for first order reactions. Introduction to Non-Ideal flow, Residence time distribution of fluid in vessels, E ,F and C curves &their relation.

cos.text: Understand the factors influencing reaction rates and analyze reaction mechanisms.
Interpret kinetic data using integral and differential methods for various reaction orders.
Understand about reactor analysis and design.
Decide the type of reactors and their arrangement of reactors for best performance.
Analyse the effect of temperature and pressure on the reaction kinetics
Analyze non-ideal flow patterns using residence time distribution and related curves.

objectives_print: To impart the basic concepts of Chemical Reaction Engineering
To develop understanding about reactor analysis, performance and design.
To develop understanding of Reaction Kinetics

subjects.name: CHEMICAL ENGINEERING THERMODYNAMICS
subjects.name_print: CHEMICAL ENGINEERING THERMODYNAMICS (scheme row 'BCH 505'; detail header 'COURSETITLE:CHEMICAL ENGINEERING THERMODYNAMICS')
subjects.marks_print: 20 10 30 | 70 | 100 (CT TA Total | TE | Total); header columns CT TA Total PS TE PE

units.1: Basic concepts in Thermodynamics, laws of Thermodynamics and their applications in engineering problems, steady flow processes, unsteady flow processes, entropy and entropy balance for open systems
units.2: An introduction to vapor-liquid Equilibria, qualitative behavior of the vapour-liquid equilibria (VLE), simple models for vapor-liquid equilibria, Raoults law, Henry’s law, Dew point and Bubble point calculations, VLE by modified Raoults law, the gamma/Philips formulation of VLE
units.3: Solution Thermodynamics- Fundamental property relay, Chemical potential, partial molar Property, partial properties in binary solutions, equations relating molar and partial molar properties, criteria for Equilibrium between phases in multicomponent non reacting systems in terms of chemical potential, fugacity and fugacity coefficient for pure species, fugacity and fugacity coefficient for species in solutions, fugacity coefficient from the virial equation of state and generalized correlations
units.4: Solution Thermodynamics Applications- ideal solution, Lewis rand all rule, excess Gibbs energy and activity coefficient, Liquid phase properties from VLE data, Excess Gibbs energy data reduction, Thermodynamic consistency of phase equilibria, applications of the correlations and prediction of phase equilibria, models for excess Gibbs energy, Property change of mixing
units.5: Chemical Reaction Equilibria-The reaction coordinate, standard Gibbs free energy change and Equilibrium constant, Effect of temperature on Equilibrium constant, evaluation of Equilibrium constant, relation of equilibrium constants to composition for gas phase and liquid phase reactions, Equilibrium conversion for single reaction, Thermodynamic analysis of simultaneous reactions

cos.text: Understand and apply the fundamental laws of thermodynamics to engineering problems.
Analyze vapor-liquid equilibria using Raoult's law, Henry's law, and modified Raoult's law.
Evaluate solution thermodynamics, including chemical potential and partial molar properties, in multi-component systems.
Apply thermodynamic models to predict phase equilibria and assess excess Gibbs energy in mixtures.
Determine equilibrium constants and analyze the impact of temperature on chemical reaction equilibria.
Perform thermodynamic analysis of single and simultaneous reactions to evaluate equilibrium conversion.

objectives_print: To understand the laws of Thermodynamics in solving problems
To impart fundamental concepts of solution Thermodynamics to describe& predict phase equilibria
To understand the functional relationship between Chemical Reactions and Thermodynamics

units.1:
1. Basic considerations: Aims and objectives of preservation & processing of foods, Wastage of Foods, Food Safety and Food Security, Causes of quality deterioration and spoilage of perishable foods
